raw_response:
## My thinking this year

I'm 60 now, been at this 40 years, and I've been growing chrysanthemum on my 35 mu for long enough to know what this crop demands. My household is just me — my wife passed some years back, my children work in the city — so everything beyond my own two hands means hiring people. That's the biggest cost factor I deal with, bigger than fertilizer by far.

Chrysanthemum isn't wheat or maize. It's a cash crop, labor-intensive, especially at picking. One mu of chrysanthemum needs maybe 20-30 person-days across the season when you count transplanting, weeding, pinching, and the multiple flower harvests. On 35 mu that's 700-1000 person-days I can't do alone. I budget for it.

With my background I think about this systematically. I target around 120-140 kg dried flowers per mu — that's a realistic yield for the varieties we grow here (mostly 北京菊 and 怀菊 types) on decent land with well irrigation. Price last year was around 45-55 yuan/kg for middle-grade dried flower; I plan assuming 45 to be safe.

**Land preparation & planting:** I prepare the land in March with deep plowing and incorporate well-rotted manure — about 2000 kg/mu, I get this from the cattle operation in the next village for around 150 yuan/mu delivered. I transplant cuttings in late April when soil temperature stabilizes above 12°C. I buy cuttings from a propagator in Anguo — mother stock matters for flower quality. About 4000 plants per mu, roughly 0.15 yuan each, so 600 yuan/mu just for planting material. That's a serious investment but saved cuttings give inconsistent flower grade and my buyers pay by grade.

**Fertilizer plan:** Base fertilizer: compound 15-15-15 at 40 kg/mu before transplanting, plus the manure providing slow-release N and micronutrients. Topdress at branching (late June) with urea 10 kg/mu, and again at bud initiation (late August) with a potassium-heavy NPK — say 10-10-30 at 15 kg/mu. Total synthetic N works out to roughly 12 kg/mu, P around 8 kg/mu, K around 11 kg/mu. I go lighter on N than people think because too much N on chrysanthemum grows leaves and delays flowering — I learned that lesson years ago.

**Irrigation:** Well water, metered electricity. I irrigate after transplanting, then roughly every 15-20 days through July-August, then carefully around bud formation and flowering — water stress at bud stage kills flower quality. Maybe 6 irrigations total. I stop watering 10 days before harvest to concentrate the flowers.

**Pest management:** Aphids are the big one, plus thrips and leaf rust in humid weeks. I do 4-5 sprays across the season — imidacloprid rotation for aphids, a triazole for rust when I see it. I don't spray preventively; I walk the fields and decide. Pesticide cost maybe 80 yuan/mu.

**Harvest:** Pickings start mid-October and go through mid-November, typically 3-4 rounds as flowers mature. This is where labor crushes you — hired pickers at 120-150 yuan/day, and you need them fast because overripe flowers lose grade. I plan 12-15 hired days per mu just for picking, plus drying-shed labor.

**Risk thinking:** Price is my main worry, not yield. The flos market swings. I'm keeping a little cash reserve and not expanding acreage this year — 35 mu is already stretching my management bandwidth alone. If prices crash I'll still cover costs at 40 yuan/kg.
